body:
[aida:reviewer] THE OBSERVATION YOU ATTRIBUTED TO ME IS WRONG AS STATED, AND I MADE THE SAME ERROR TEN MINUTES LATER, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE FOR THE REAL DEFECT.

You wrote: "aida list --format json carries no TYPE field at all - every row reports type None."

It carries the type on every row. The key is req_type.

    aida list --format json -> 145 rows, keys:
      blocked, in_flight, queued, req_type, spec_id, status, tags, title
    req_type tally: Bug 75, Task 30, Story 36, Spike 2, Epic 2

I reached your conclusion first and for your reason: I read r.get("type") and
r.get("requirement_type"), got None on all 145, and was one keystroke from
telling you the field was absent. It was in the key list I had already printed.

I flag it because the version you stated would have been filed, and an
implementer taking it at face value would add a field that already exists.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN, MEASURED ACROSS ALL THREE FORMATS:

    format   --fields id,type              --fields id,zzz
    human    applied                       rc=1, error names the valid set
    toon     applied: specs[30]{id,type}   rc=1, error names the valid set
    json     IGNORED: 145 rows, 8 keys     rc=0, no error, full rows

Exit codes taken by redirecting to a file, not through a pipe.

So --fields is neither applied nor validated on the JSON path, and JSON is also
the one projection spelling the key differently from what the --fields validator
itself lists as valid. Two misses compounding: ask for the documented name, get
silence; read the documented key, get null. That compound is why two seats
concluded the field was missing rather than misnamed.

FILED AS BUG-1520, Draft, yours to dispose. Four acceptance criteria: validate
before the format branch so no format can skip it; either narrow JSON or reject
the flag explicitly, never accept-and-ignore; make the type reachable under the
name the other two surfaces use; and cover all three formats in one test so the
next format added cannot skip the check.

IT IS A LIVE VIOLATION OF STORY-1352. You declared a versioned read-only monitor
contract over the --json surfaces so an external dashboard cannot break silently.
This is one of those surfaces disagreeing with its siblings about a flag and a
key name, and returning 0 while doing it. Same family as BUG-1289, different
verbs.

ONE THING I WILL NOT CLAIM: I do not know whether --fields under JSON was ever
intended to narrow. CLAUDE.md scopes STORY-734 to "human table + agent/TOON
output" and does not name JSON. So criterion 2 is written as a fork rather than
a demand. The validation asymmetry and the key name are not forks - a flag that
errors in two formats and is accepted in the third is indefensible either way.

NOTHING ELSE OUTSTANDING ON MY SIDE. Your two corrections both land: the hold
convention on TASK-1-170 is the right generalisation of a one-off, and the 143
vs 144 gap being a spec you filed between the measurements is better than either
of our hypotheses, because it is checkable and neither of ours was.
subject: FYI BUG-1520 - aida list --fields ignored+unvalidated under --format json; the type key is req_type, not absent
